subject: Request: security playbook + initial notification and postmortem follow-up

Cc: security@finsecure.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: incident response playbook and notification process

Hi Ben,

Hope you’re well. As part of our ongoing vendor review for SOC 2 readiness we need your incident response playbook and a short note on how Redwood handles initial customer notifications for security incidents (timing, criteria for notification, communication templates). FinSecure is particularly interested in:

- The escalation path (on-call, security ops, legal, customer success)
- Notification SLA (target time-to-notify after detection)
- What you share in an initial notification vs. a full postmortem
- Any standard evidence artifacts (logs, timeline exports, IR checklists) you can provide for SOC 2 reviewers

We can accept a redacted playbook and a short example notification template. If possible, please send by end of day today — our audit window opens next week.

Thanks,
Asha Desai
Sr. Security Operations Manager | FinSecure, Inc.
asha.desai@finsecure.com
+1 (415) 555-0107

Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 11:07:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: incident response playbook and notification process

Asha —

Thanks for the note. Attaching our redacted Incident Response Playbook (internal links removed) and a short template we use for initial customer notifications. Highlights below:

- Escalation: on-call -> Security Ops -> Incident Lead -> Legal & CS within 30 mins of classification as P1/P2.
- Notification SLA: initial customer notification target is 60–120 minutes after a confirmed-impact detection (can be faster for clear-cut cases).
- Initial notification contents: brief summary, affected services, immediate mitigation, known impact (if any), and next steps/timeline for a fuller update.
- Evidence: we provide a timeline export (CSV), request/response logs (redacted by default), and a signed manifest for SOC 2 reviewers.

We included a compact playbook (Redwood_IR_Playbook_v1.3.pdf) and an evidence manifest template (soc2_evidence_manifest.xlsx). If you need anything more specific for the SIG or CAIQ, tell me which control IDs and we’ll extract the artifacts.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachment: Redwood_IR_Playbook_v1.3.pdf (application/pdf, 1.2MB); soc2_evidence_manifest.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 85KB)

Subject: RE: Request: incident response playbook and notification process

Ben — quick internal update to thread. We just triaged an anomaly in the EU inference cluster that flagged as an integrity check failure (internal ticket INC-20260325-07). On initial review:

- Impact: short-lived disruption for a subset of requests in eu-west-1, 10:13–10:45 UTC. No evidence of data exfiltration; KV cache was restarted.
- Classification: P2 (service impact, no confirmed data exposure).
- Actions: on-call patched and remediated within 20 minutes; full node replacement performed.
- Next steps: security ops running a post-incident timeline export and will collect relevant logs for SOC 2 artifacts.

If you want to share an initial, we should be transparent but careful not to include logs in the first message — those go to SOC reviewers under an NDA. I can assemble a short notification template specific to this event for Asha.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Staff Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Follow-up: incident update and postmortem (INC-20260325-07)

Asha —

Wanted to follow up with a formal update on the incident Hannah flagged yesterday and to share the postmortem and evidence manifest for your SOC 2 review.

Summary (INC-20260325-07):
- Window: 2026-03-25 10:13–10:45 UTC
- Impact: transient request failures affecting ~0.4% of customer traffic routed through eu-west-1. No customer data was accessed outside normal request processing; no indications of exfiltration.
- Root cause: memory leak in a third-party shard manager triggered periodic GC storms leading to node restarts.
- Mitigation: restart and node replacement, patch applied to the shard manager. Monitoring rules updated to detect GC patterns earlier.
- Customer notification: initial notification provided within 80 minutes of detection; follow-up postmortem prepared and attached.

Attachments: postmortem_finsecure_20260325.pdf (detailed timeline, impact matrix, remediation & mitigations) and soc2_evidence_manifest.xlsx (redacted request logs + timeline export for reviewer ingestion). We can provide more granular logs to your SOC reviewer under the NDA and SFTP link — let us know the contact and we’ll provision access.

If you’d prefer a canned notification for your audit pack (short summary + statement of no data exposure), we included a one-paragraph template in the postmortem. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the artifacts.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
